# Incident Report — MTA 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Evidence:** `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,091 packets, 2024-09-04 21:32:31 to 22:32:07 UTC, SHA256 `8fee06d0b1686faab4364f5b7a741e736ad7e713d5ca9299ff9161a4b4d4862e`), plus exported Suricata/IDS alert log and screenshot from the same directory. Analysis performed with tshark against the pcap; findings cross-checked against the alert export.

## Infected host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.17.0.99 |
| MAC address | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 (Intel NIC), confirmed via DHCP and ARP |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (seen in DHCP Option 12, NBNS name registration, and DNS A-record self-registration to `bepositive.com`) |
| Windows domain | BEPOSITIVE.COM (AD domain; domain controller WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19 at 172.17.0.17) |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** — observed as the CNameString in multiple Kerberos AS-REQ exchanges with the BEPOSITIVE.COM KDC starting at t=+243.98s |

172.17.0.17 is the internal domain controller/DNS server, not an attacker system. The GPL alerts naming 172.17.0.99 → 172.17.0.17 ("SMB Session Setup NTLMSSP overflow", "SMB IPC$ unicode share access", "SMB_COM_TRANSACTION Max Data Count of 0", "RPC kerberos principal overflow") all fall on legitimate SMB/Kerberos domain-authentication traffic to the DC and are legacy-signature false positives, not exploitation, based on packet content review.

## Malware family and attribution

**Koi Stealer** (also tracked as Koi Loader/Stealer in the Proofpoint/ET naming convention).

- **Signature-confirmed**: the Suricata alert export contains `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (48 hits) firing on 172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197:80 POST /foots.php traffic, corroborated by `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser 1` (50 hits) on the same stream.
- **Behavioral corroboration** observed directly in the pcap:
  - Beaconing begins at t=+155.9s with three rapid POSTs to `/foots.php`, each carrying a pipe-delimited body, e.g. `101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=` (bot ID | campaign/machine GUID | session token | base64-like encrypted blob).
  - A follow-up GET `/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` returns a plaintext config string `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`, after which the malware POSTs 105 bytes of binary/encrypted data to `/index.php` (bot-ID/subID/URL structured C2 protocol).
  - After the initial handshake, the host beacons to `/foots.php` on a steady ~70–90 second interval for the entire remainder of the capture (last beacon at t=+3564.6s, capture ends at t=3576.2s) — continuous C2 check-in behavior.
  - All traffic to the C2 is HTTP to a bare dotted-quad IP with a spoofed legacy IE7/.NET user-agent string (`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; ...)`), and no DNS lookup was ever performed for 79.124.78.197 — the address is hardcoded in the sample.
- No dropper executable or clearly identifiable stage-1 payload is visible in this pcap (capture starts at host boot/DHCP-Discover, so initial delivery predates or falls outside the capture window). A TLS 1.3 session to 46.254.34.201 (SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`) opens at t=+153.3s, two seconds before the first C2 beacon, and moves 701 KB to the host over ~102 seconds — timing consistent with a stage-1 loader fetch, but content is unobservable due to TLS encryption, so this is a behavioral/timing observation only, not confirmed.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- `79.124.78.197:80` (HTTP) — primary Koi Stealer C2, confirmed by ETPRO signature
- `46.254.34.201:443` (TLS 1.3, SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`) — probable stage-1 payload delivery infrastructure (behavioral/timing correlation only, not signature-confirmed)

**Malicious URLs / endpoints**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — repeated C2 check-in/beacon endpoint
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — secondary C2 endpoint (config retrieval + encrypted data POST)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — observed config-pull request; returned subid/URL string above

**Malicious domain**
- `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (TLS SNI only, resolved via 46.254.34.201) — treat as suspect delivery infrastructure pending further review; no supporting DNS query for this name was captured (SNI came from an already-established connection outside/at capture start)

**Files / hashes**
- No executable, script, or document payload with recoverable content was transferred in this capture (the only binary data observed — the 94-byte and 105-byte POST bodies to `/foots.php` and `/index.php` — is encrypted C2 telemetry, not a retrievable file). Consequently **no file names or SHA256 hashes of malware artifacts can be grounded in this evidence.** If a dropper/loader binary exists, it was delivered before this capture began or over the encrypted 46.254.34.201 session and is not recoverable from this pcap alone.

**Not attributed to the malware** (reviewed and excluded)
- `acroipm2.adobe.com` GET `/assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt` (23.220.251.47) — legitimate Adobe Acrobat/Reader update-manager check-in; shares the same spoofed legacy user-agent by coincidence of that Adobe component, unrelated destination/IP infrastructure to the C2.
- All `*.bepositive.com`, `*.microsoft.com`, `*.msn.com`, `windowsupdate.com`, `lencr.org`, `msftconnecttest.com` traffic — normal AD-joined Windows enterprise workstation background traffic.
